The graph above shows a portion of the curve $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ and the line $y=2.$ The expressions 

$$
x={\theta }_{1}+n\cdot b,\,x={\theta }_{2}+n\cdot b,
$$

where ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2}$ and $n$ is an integer, generate the $x$-values of all of the points of intersection. Find the values of ${\theta }_{1}$ and ${\theta }_{2}$ in $[0,{360}^{∘}),$ and the value of $b.$

worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡x=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ therefore the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})={60}^{∘}.
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the $4$th quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13994895/assets/40879eca8abd0b5b45d233a6aafe8642a10aaa7cf91b090bee86b47333beb0b8.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={360}^{∘}-{60}^{∘} \\  & ={300}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution for the given equation is 

$$
x={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},\,x=-{60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.
$$

Writing this as $x=\theta +n\cdot {360}^{∘},$ where $\theta \in [0,{360}^{∘}),$ we get

$$
x={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},\,x={300}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.
$$

Therefore, since ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2},$ we have ${\theta }_{1}=60\,{\,}^{∘},$ ${\theta }_{2}=300\,{\,}^{∘},$ and $b=360\,{\,}^{∘}.$

EXPLANATION

At the intersection points, the y-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation sec⁡x=2.

Recall that sec⁡x=1cos⁡x, therefore the given equation is equivalent to cos⁡x=12.

First, we find the principal value:

x1=arccos⁡(12)=60∘.

Our first solution lies in the 1st quadrant and has a reference angle of θR=60∘. Since cos⁡x<0, the second solution must lie in the 4th quadrant, and it also has θR=60∘.

Since the second solution x2 lies in the 4th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

x2=360∘−θR=360∘−60∘=300∘

The general solution for the given equation is x=60∘+n⋅360∘,x=−60∘+n⋅360∘.

Writing this as x=θ+n⋅360∘, where θ∈[0,360∘), we get x=60∘+n⋅360∘,x=300∘+n⋅360∘.

Therefore, since θ1<θ2, we have θ1=60∘, θ2=300∘, and b=360∘.
